chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from the one who narrated it to him, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, who said:
I said to Abī al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام): “It has been narrated to us from Abī ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) that he said:”
“Indeed, our knowledge is ghabir, and mazbūr, and a marking in the hearts, and a tapping in the ears.”

So he said: “As for al-ghābir, it is what has preceded from our knowledge; as for al-mazbūr, it is what comes to us; as for the marking in the hearts, it is inspiration; and as for the tapping in the ears, it is the command of the angel.”

key_terms.أَمْرُ الْمَلَكِ: the command or communication of the angel
key_terms.النَّقْرُ فِي الْأَسْمَاعِ: a tapping or striking in the ears; a mode of reception through hearing
key_terms.النَّكْتُ فِي الْقُلُوبِ: an inward casting or marking in hearts, explained here as inspiration
key_terms.عِلْمَنَا: our knowledge; the divinely granted knowledge of the Imams (عليهم السلام)
key_terms.غَابِرٌ: that which has preceded; earlier transmitted knowledge
key_terms.مَزْبُورٌ: that which comes to them; inscribed or conveyed knowledge

ai.seo_question: What do غَابِرٌ, مَزْبُورٌ, نَكْتٌ فِي الْقُلُوبِ, and نَقْرٌ فِي الْأَسْمَاعِ mean in the knowledge of the Imams (عليهم السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith explains categories of the knowledge of the Imams (عليهم السلام), distinguishing between what has preceded, what comes to them, inward inspiration in hearts, and the angel’s communication in hearing. It highlights the divinely granted and multi-faceted nature of their knowledge within Shia theology.
